In Arabic P. Lent. is also called ضرو [ḍirw]. Nuwairī [=an-Nuwairī, Nihāyat al-arab] in E. Wiedem. [=Eilhard Wiedemann, Beiträge zur Geschichte der Naturwissenschaften] 49, 21 says that kamkām is the lentiscus resin of the tree ḍirw, according to others its leaves or bark. It flows out elastic, black as pitch. The tree resembles the terebinth, buṭm, according to others a very large oak, but is said to be smoother and more delicate. It bears clusters of fruit, like the buṭm. Used for toothpicks: Silberberg, Dināwarī [=Silberberg, Das Pflanzenbuch des ad-Dīnawarī] 78.

The midrash cited renders the bibl. [=biblical] lōṭ as mastic: מסטוכי (LA. [=variant reading] מסטכי, מסתיכי, corrupt. [=corrupted] מפטדי, correctly RDK. [=Rabbi David Kimhi, Sefer ha-Shorashim] sv. [=sub voce] lōṭ: מוצטכא) and adds: עבידא כול (LAA. [=variant readings] according to Albeck's [=Chanoch Albeck, co-editor of Bereshit Rabba, private communication]*) communication: עבידה בול, יעבידא כיל, עבירא כול, עביד הביל), which is probably meant to signify “in little lumps”. Menaḥem b. Salomo [=Menaḥem ben Salomo, author of Sechel tob] (1139) says: mustichi is like frankincense and consists of small grains like grains of salt.

In the Tannaitic period mastic was chewed in Palestine, either as a remedy or — as still today (Luncz zu Farḥi [=Luncz's notes to Estori ha-Farḥi, Kaftor wa-feraḥ] p. [=page] 662) — to improve the breath — εὐωδία [euōdia] Diosk. [=Dioscorides, De materia medica] 1, 93 Spr. [=edition by Sprengel] 1, 67 W. [=edition by Wellmann] (Preuss [=Preuss, Biblisch-talmudische Medizin] 195) TSabb. [=Tosefta, tractate Shabbat] 12, 127_{8} מסטיכי (LA. מוסתכין, Maim. [=Maimonides] מסטכי, Codd. [=codices] מצטכי**) Maim. H. Sabb. [=Hilkhot Shabbat] 21, 24)***). Tur [=Arbaʿa Ṭurim] SchA. [=Shulchan Arukh] OCh. [=Oraḥ Ḥayyim] 216, 3. 328, 36.: It may not be used as a remedy on the Sabbath, but it may be used as a cosmetic.

ZDMG. [=Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenländischen Gesellschaft] 28, 702 Kautchuk Persan ḳenderan. Orientals like to produce a greater secretion of saliva by chewing resinous substances, such as mastic, pistachio resin (sakkis). Ḳenderan is used, a rubber-like mass made from the thickened latex of several species of Scorzonera and Podospermum.

Aßaf (161 Venetianer) [=Venetianer, Asaf Judaeus], in his excerpt from the syr. [=Syriac] Diosk., calls the mastic tree the tree of the small black pistachios, which grows in Šārōn (read with Venetianer: Chios) and exudes mastic. It is called gr. [=Greek] chīnos, lat. From a commentary on B. r. Albeck [=Chanoch Albeck, co-editor of Bereshit Rabba] cites as an explanation of mastic: מושנא or מוסכא, which rests on confusion with musco, muschio, musk. מוסכי in Alfassi [=Isaac Alfasi, Halakhot] on Sabb. [=tractate Shabbat] is probably merely a miswriting of mastic; it has been corrected by ב״ח [=Bayit Ḥadash by Joel Sirkes].
Likewise RMbN. [=Nachmanides, Commentary on the Torah] Ki tissa 76^{b}_{21}. B. r. 91, 11 LA: מסטיכי, מוסטכי; מסטכי, מסתיכי, מצטוכי, מצטוכא, מצטכא.

Tanḥūm [=Tanḥum ha-Yerushalmi, al-Murshid al-kāfī] remarks on this that Maimūnī retains the Mishnaic word, which Tanḥūm considers an Arabic loanword, because he knows no certain Hebrew designation (Bacher, Tanchum [=Bacher, Aus dem Wörterbuche Tanchum Jeruschalmi's] 80).
